def: The part of the body that contains digestive organs bounded between the diaphragm and the pelvis. It is more commonly referred to as the stomach.
This treatment strives to stop a migraine before or right after it starts. People may administer these types of medication in pill-form through the mouth, skin patches, nasal spray, and more.

An area that is damaged. An eye abrasion refers to any area on or around the eye that suffers a bruise, laceration or any other form of damage. The severity of an abrasion varies based on the cause of the injury.

The decision of abstaining from sexual intercourse or sexual activity. It is the only birth control method that is 100% effective in preventing pregnancy and STDs or STIs when all sexual contact, including vaginal, oral, and anal sex is avoided.
Any injury to the inner ear, usually due to exposure to high-decibel noise.
Also referred to as a chest cold, acute bronchitis is a short-term infection treated with medication. Acute bronchitis is not usually as severe as chronic bronchitis.
Healthcare services or treatments in which a patient receives short-term care for an illness or injury.
An illness that has a sudden onset, but does not usually last long.
A type of ear infection that affects the middle ear.
Back pain directly related to soft tissue damage. Typically lasts three to six months or less. Resolves itself gradually as the injured tissues heal.
An asthma diagnosis that occurs after the age of 20. Asthma in adulthood is typically caused by infection, exercise, allergens, and air pollution (an irritant).
A form of asthma that occurs when asthmatic symptoms arise after breathing in allergens that trigger asthma, such as pollen, dust mites, and mold.
A condition in which the immune system overcorrects or otherwise reacts abnormally to a foreign substance. These substances, known as antigens, are typically harmless.
A reaction to a specific substance in which the body rejects the substance believing it is harmful to the body. Allergic reactions are a common reason one may experience a sinus infection.
A condition in which the immune system overcorrects or otherwise reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

A condition that causes the partial or total loss of memories, such as facts, information, or experiences, and results in difficulty learning new information or remembering past events or information.
The most severe form of an allergic reaction, which causes swelling, low blood pressure, bluish skin, shock, and extreme difficulty in breathing.
A condition in which the blood is lacking adequate healthy red blood cells.

A symptom of coronary heart disease that is caused by a reduced blood flow to the heart. It has many of the same symptoms as a heart attack, although it is less severe and can serve as a warning sign of a future heart attack if not treated.
An eating disorder in which the person severely restricts their intake of food.
A treatment option used to reduce inflammation. Anti-inflammatory medications are often used to treat bruising, especially bruises caused by a physical injury.
A style of eating that includes foods that decrease inflammation and excludes foods that encourage inflammation.
A medication that destroys or slows the growth of bacteria that cause infection
A popular treatment method for bacterial infections. Since antibiotics do not work to treat viral infections, they are useless as it pertains to the common cold and flu.
A substance, such as insulin or an oral diabetes medication, that helps diabetics control their blood sugar levels.
Drugs that treat various allergies by dampening the effects of histamine at certain cell receptors.
A group of medications used to treat parasitic diseases and infections, such as lice.
A type of medication used to treat viral infections.
A form of treatment for viral infections such as influenza. Since antibiotics do not work with the cold or flu, antiviral medications are the preferred medication for both.
A condition in which the appendix becomes severely inflamed and filled with pus, causing severe abdominal pain. Appendicitis usually requires immediate surgery.
A condition in which one or more joints becomes inflamed and tender.
A condition in which the airways are tightened, producing extra mucus and making it difficult to breathe. This causes asthmatic symptoms such as coughing, wheezing, and shortness of breath.

A triggered reaction in which the airways become swollen, inflamed, and contracted, making it difficult to breathe. During an asthma attack, thicker mucus is produced that can block the airways entirely.
A diagnosis that indicates an individual has both asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) symptoms.
Atypical pneumonia affects the lower respiratory tract. It does not usually cause severe symptoms, making it more challenging to diagnose than other forms of pneumonia.

A measurement of a person’s range of sense of hearing. An audiometry test involves the use of playing different sound frequencies into a set of headphones and testing whether or not the individual heard the sound(s).
A sensation that is often experienced right before a migraine attack. An aura is typically considered a warning sign that a migraine is about to take place and presents itself in various ways.
Single-celled organisms or microbes found almost everywhere on earth. Though bacteria are essential to Earth’s ecosystems, pathogenic bacteria may cause infection or otherwise cause illness.
A disease caused by microorganisms that invade tissues and trigger a protective immune response.

A test used to assess an athlete’s balance and brain function (including learning and memory skills, ability to pay attention or concentrate, and how quickly he or she thinks and solves problems), as well as for the presence of any concussion symptoms.
An eating disorder in which the person binge eats without a feeling of self-control.
Any method, including medications, procedures, devices, and behaviors, used to prevent pregnancy.
The bladder is responsible for collecting and holding urine until it is ready to leave the body through the urethra.
The inability to see in one of both eyes due to an eye injury, genetics, disease, or condition.
The act of blood turning from a liquid to a gel, which can cause severe medical complications. Blood clots can form from bruises, which is why proper bruise treatment is important.
The pressure of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries.
Medicines that work in different ways to lower blood pressure by keeping the blood vessels from narrowing or preventing calcium from entering the muscle cells of the heart and blood vessels.

The dual measurement that records blood pressure. The first number, called systolic blood pressure, measures the pressure in the arteries when the heart beats. The second number, called diastolic blood pressure, measures the pressure in the arteries when the heart rests between beats.

Blood sugar testing can be useful in both diagnosing and managing diabetes. By regularly testing their blood sugar levels, patients can monitor the effects of their medications, track their treatment progress, and more.

A laboratory test done by drawing an individual’s blood, often through the vein with the use of a needle, and sent to a laboratory to test for any abnormalities or the existence of a harmful infection.
A form of medication that helps treat and prevent blood clots from occurring. In some instances, blood thinners are prescribed to deal with bruising.
A person’s BMI is the weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters. A high BMI can indicate high body fatness.
Refers to how warm or cold our body is. The average body temperature is generally believed to be 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit, although everyone’s average body temperature may differ slightly.
A term used to describe a shot that is administered after an initial shot is given to help support the immune system in the long term.
A form of cognitive dysfunction that manifests in the form of memory problems, poor concentration, lack of mental clarity, and inability to focus.
Often confused with bronchitis, bronchiectasis is a condition in which the lungs become damaged. Although they both affect the lungs, bronchitis is a different disease than bronchiectasis.
Inflammation of the bronchial tube lining which are responsible for carrying air to and from the lungs.
A skin injury often results due to trauma, although it can occur for many different reasons. Blood gathers underneath the skin after a bruise, which causes the discoloration of the skin.
An eating disorder in which the person purges after binge eating.
The name for a group of diseases involving abnormal, malignant cell growth that may spread to or invade other parts of the body.
The cervical spine houses the spinal cord and sends messages from the brain to different parts of the body.
The front of the body between the neck and abdomen wherein resides the heart and lungs.

A specialist who diagnoses and treats the body’s muscular, nervous, and skeletal systems. Also known as chiropractic physicians or doctors of chiropractic, chiropractors typically have a special focus on back and neck pain. They may use electric, heat, light, massage, ultrasound, and water therapy to treat back pain.
A fatty or lipid substance found throughout the body that aids in producing hormones and vitamins. There are both good and bad cholesterol which can be naturally-produced or consumed through food.

In most cases, chronic bronchitis is much more severe than acute bronchitis as the treatment for it is more challenging. Chronic bronchitis usually results from constant damage to the lungs (e.g., smoking).
Medical care that aims to treat pre-existing or long-term illnesses, such as diabetes or cancer.
A chronic condition or disease is a condition that is persistent or has long-lasting effects over time.
A disease or illness lasting one or more years, requires ongoing medical care, or affects daily activities of the affected person.
An illness that develops slowly and can worsen over time, for weeks or years.
Diseases that block the airways and make it difficult to breathe.

Back pain that lasts for longer than three months. May gradually become worse and recur periodically, even after the tissues have healed and for no apparent reason. Commonly associated with lower back pain, headache, and arthritic pain.
A pattern of headaches that happen in close proximity to one another. Cluster headaches often involve several headaches occurring within a span of one month.
Also commonly referred to as mental exertion, this term describes mental focus. After a concussion, individuals typically have difficulty with cognitive exertion.
A type of psycho-social intervention that focuses on changing cognitive distortions and behaviors, enhancing emotional regulation, and developing personal coping strategies.

A procedure in which a medical professional examines the inside of the colon in order to determine any irregularities that may exist, in order to treat or prevent serious illnesses or conditions from occurring.
A common viral infection involving the inflammation of the mucous membrane of the nose and throat.
A condition that occurs simultaneously with another.
A blood test that provides information about the counts of white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets, the concentration of hemoglobin, and the hematocrit.
A condition in which the nerve roots in the spinal cord are pinched or irritated. The pain associated with compressed nerves is also known as sciatica or radicular pain.
A non-invasive X-ray scan of the body or part of the body that uses several X-rays to create detailed structures of the inside of the body.
A type of traumatic brain injury caused by an impact to the head or an impact to the body that causes the head and brain to move rapidly. It may occur with or without loss of consciousness.
The state of having a disease, illness, injury, defect, or disorder and is typically being treated by a medical professional.

The state of having an unclear state of mind. A fever that leads to dehydration can result in confusion, which should be treated as a highly concerning symptom. Confusion may also be a sign of a concussion.
The state of being congested; occurs when the sinuses are blocked, making it difficult to breathe normally.
The clear, thin membrane covering part of the front surface of the eye and lining the inside of the eyelids. The conjunctiva protects the eye from microbes.
A condition that leads to an inability to produce a bowel movement. Constipation usually causes discomfort in the abdomen region, and it can often be treated with laxatives.
This term is used to describe a rash that develops as a result of contact with a particular substance. The substance can either be the main cause of the rash or trigger an allergic reaction.
A state of impurity in which pollution or poisoning spoils or infects an environment, physical body, or consumable product.
Also known as contrast agents or contrast media. Ingested to improve X-ray images and facilitate the radiologist in distinguishing normal and abnormal conditions from each other.
A contusion, particularly one that occurs on the eye, is a bruise around the eye that often results in a black eye. A contusion occurs after suffering a blow to the eye.

A rupturing or penetration to the cornea, which is the outermost layer of the eye that helps protect the eye. A corneal perforation can happen for a number of reasons, ranging from being hit by an object to a papercut.
The body’s main stress hormone; can contribute to body fat accumulation.
A cough is the body pushing air out of your lungs quickly to get rid of an irritant
An inflammatory bowel disease that causes severe abdominal pain that often leads to diarrhea. Crohn’s disease can affect anyone, regardless of age.
Stands for computerized tomography scan. Utilizes computer processing and a series of X-ray images taken from different angles to create more detailed, cross-sectional images.
To bring about recovery from a disease or condition and rid the body of it.
A condition where an individual continually experiences episodes of vomiting without a clear, defined cause, although in some the cause may be apparent.
A genetic condition that causes damage to the lungs and digestive system as naturally-produced fluids become thicker and more sticky, blocking the tubes, ducts, and passageways.
Cystitis refers to an infection of the urinary system, which can take place in either the lower tract or the upper tract and causes pain while urinating.
A treatment option for many types of sinus infections. A decongestant relieves nasal congestion and allows individuals suffering from sinusitis to breathe easier as they recover.
Osteoarthritis of the spine, which usually occurs in the neck or lower back.

There are three different types of burns: first degree, second degree, and third degree. A first-degree burn only burns the top layer of skin, whereas a third-degree burn can go much deeper and even reach nerves and tissue.
Dehydration is what happens to the body when it does not have enough water, preventing it from functioning properly.
A group of symptoms that affect memory, thinking, behavior, and the ability to perform everyday activities.
A skin condition that produces redness, soreness, and swelling caused by an external agent or allergic reaction
The top and second layer of skin, which is generally damaged by most rashes and burns. Our dermis and epidermis serve as the body’s first line of defense from infection.
A condition that affects the way the body processes blood sugar, although there are different types of diabetes, with different causes and symptoms.

Damaging immune system cells that may put individuals at higher risk of contracting type 1 diabetes. However, merely having diabetes autoantibodies does not guarantee that one will contract type 1 diabetes.
The identification of a problem with the human body based on the symptoms and testing procedures administered. Laboratory tests are often necessary to aid in medical diagnosis.
An umbrella term used to refer to any medical test used by practitioners to determine the seriousness and nature of a illness or condition
There are three different types of influenza (flu), influenza A, influenza B and influenza C. While each one requires treatments, some can be more serious than others.
A serious infection of the nose and throat that makes it very difficult to breathe.
A physical or mental impairment that prohibits a person from performing certain activities or participating in social interactions.
The process or state of being or becoming a color other than the original color.
A system of medical management interventions used to help patients manage an illness.
An injured joint that forces the ends of the bones from their regular positions.
A common symptom of a concussion that refers to the inability to see straight. It often is accompanied by blurred or double vision and a loss of balance, especially after a concussion.
A condition which affects a person’s relationship with food and eating.
A term used to describe a discoloration of the skin, which is typically caused by bleeding underneath the surface of the skin often due to bruising.
An itchy skin condition that often causes inflammation. Eczema, also known as atopic dermatitis, most commonly affects toddlers, and it typically appears as a rash on the arm(s).

Often referred to as an EKG or an ECG, an electrocardiogram refers to a display of an individual’s heartbeat, which is accomplished by placing devices on the chest in order to record electrical impulses of the heart.
The department of the hospital that deals with those arriving at the hospital in need of immediate care that is can be life or limb-threatening
A lung condition that occurs as a result of damaged air sacs in the lungs called alveoli. In its severe cases, emphysema can cause air sacs to rupture, making the air spaces larger.
A toxin that resides in the intestines, sometimes produced by it, and causes food poisoning symptoms and cholera.

Steroids, anesthetics, and anti-inflammatory medications are typically delivered in an epidural injection. The injection may reduce pain and swelling in and around the spinal nerve roots, as well as around damaged nerves which in time may heal.
A hormone and medication used to treat severe asthma attacks and anaphylaxis.
An epinephrine auto-injector is a device used to inject epinephrine into the body in cases of an allergic reaction or anaphylactic shock.
Bleeding from the nose caused by nose-picking, trauma, or nose conditions.
A common condition in which a male cannot achieve or maintain an erection.
A state where the penis is enlarged and rigid.

High BP in which secondary causes such as renovascular disease, renal failure, pheochromocytoma, aldosteronism, or other causes of secondary hypertension or mendelian forms (monogenic) are not present.
Hollow structures that extend from the middle ear to the pharynx (throat).
A form of asthma that occurs when the airways become narrow and inflamed during exercise, making breathing difficult.
Damage done to the eye or eye socket and surrounding areas, including tissues and bone structure, caused by a direct blow to the eye.
An eyewall injury is any damage to the outer layers of the eye, which include the sclera and cornea. An eyewall injury usually results from a blow to the eye.
Making changes to the home and common use areas with the intention of preventing falls.
A type of nutrient from animals and plants; necessary in some amounts but harmful if consumed in excess or from certain sources.
A fall that is life-threatening or causes death.
A feeling of excessive tiredness and low energy.
A birth control method in which a woman tracks the phases of her menstrual cycle in order to determine fertility and prevent or produce a pregnancy.
An above-average body temperature that is typically a sign of the body warding off an infection.
A form of medicine such as acetaminophen or Tylenol works to reduce a fever.
The use of an identified primary care source for a patient’s first healthcare visit and who remains their first point of contact when concerns arise.
Short for influenza, a highly contagious viral infection of the respiratory passages.
An annual time period that brings about an outbreak of influenza, typically during the fall and winter.
A vaccine that protects against influenza viruses.
Care gradually given to a patient after finishing initial treatment for a condition.
An illness caused by consuming foods or drinks contaminated by bacteria, toxins, parasites, or viruses.
Food intolerance occurs after eating food the body does not accept, which causes severe digestive problems such as vomiting and diarrhea.
A sickness that develops from bacteria or other harmful substances in food and causes vomiting and diarrhea.
A broken bone that punctures the skin and sometimes exposes the underlying bone.
A full-thickness burn, or third-degree burn, is one of the most serious burn types and can cause nerve damage if the burn reaches deep enough into the skin.
A type of tissue death caused by lack of blood supply, usually to the hands and feet
A deep cut or slash into the skin, which generally causes bleeding and can be painful. A gash into the skin requires prompt treatment as there is an increased risk of infection due to the open skin.
A condition, disease, or disorder that occurs in the gastrointestinal tract, such as food poisoning. The tract is a passageway from the mouth to the anus.
A branch of medicine that aims to provide high quality healthcare to elderly patients through proper diagnosis, treatment, and prevention protocol.
A medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of health conditions affecting older people.
A branch of medicine focused on all aspects of healthcare pertaining to older adults over age 65.
A type of diabetes that affects some pregnant women. Women with gestational diabetes experience rising blood sugar levels during pregnancy.
A type of sugar that acts as an energy source for the cells making up muscles and other tissues. There are two major sources of glucose: food and the liver.
A safety device that allows a person to maintain balance when attempting to sit or stand up.

There are three different degrees (or grades) of sprain and strains. A grade I strain or sprain often is not serious and suggests the ligament, muscle or tendon is only partially stretched, whereas a grade III strain may lead to a tear.
A disorder in which the body’s nerves are attacked by the immune system.
A flexible splint used to immobilize, stabilize, and support dislocations, fractures, and injuries.
A safety device, most commonly used in the shower, that a person holds on to in an easy-slip space.
A fixed railing that supports people who cannot easily balance when standing or moving.
A potential source of harm that could cause serious injury or death.
A symptom that describes pain anywhere in the head or neck region. A headache often accompanies a fever, especially when associated with an infection or heat exhaustion.
A complete, or very close to complete, blockage of blood flow to the heart. A heart attack is a serious emergency and requires a 911 call as soon as possible.
A condition of the heart that results in a diseased vessel, structural problem, or blood clot. A heart attack is one example of heart disease.
A machine that displays a patient’s heart rhythm through wires that run from patches placed on the patient’s chest
This term refers to the feeling that your heart has either skipped a heartbeat or experienced an additional heartbeat.
A burning sensation felt in the chest, behind the breastbone, often resulting from acid regurgitation into the esophagus, commonly known as indigestion.
Heat exhaustion is an illness that occurs after a person has been exposed to high temperatures.

A condition in which the outer portion of the vertebral disc is torn, causing the inner portion to extrude. This condition can compress the surrounding nerves and create radiating pain through the back. The pain may also affect the arms and legs.
A condition in which a rubber-like disc slips out in between two spinal bones.
A health condition in which large amounts of bad cholesterol are found in the bad, which may lead to more serious health complications, including heart and artery disease.
Histamines are organic nitrogenous compounds involved in local immune responses and inflammatory responses, such as itching.
A simply prepared remedy administered without professional supervision or prescription.
A device that keeps air in a room moist.
An intravenous fluid (IV) that delivers fluids directly to the bloodstream, especially in cases of dehydration or loss of essential vitamins and nutrients.
A condition in which the force of blood against the artery walls is too high.
A natural, physical reaction that occurs when a foreign substance unrecognizable by the immune system invades the body.
The ability of the immune system to fight off and resist a particular form of infection. One who is immune to an infection has ‘built up an immunity’ toward that particular bacteria or virus.
An immunization is the injection of a substance into the body, such as influenza, to help the body build up an immunity to the bacteria or virus.
A vaccination or immunization is the injection of a substance into the body, such as influenza, used to help the body build up an immunity to the bacteria or virus.
A term used to describe when a bacteria, virus or other harmful substance enters the body. An infection can develop when a cut is not adequately treated, leaving the skin open and vulnerable.
A response to cellular injury in which part of the body becomes reddened, swollen, hot, and often painful.
Most commonly referred to as the flu, influenza is a viral infection that causes symptoms of a runny nose, constant coughing, chills, fatigue and fever. It can be treated with medical assistance.
A common condition that causes the corner or side of the toenail grows into the flesh.
The part of the ear at the end of the ear tubes. Separated into three main parts: cochlea, semicircular canals, and vestibule.
What they call a person when they are staying in the hospital to receive medical care.
Insomnia is a common sleep disorder that causes people to have difficulty with falling asleep, staying asleep, waking up too early, and not being able to fall back asleep.
A naturally occurring hormone produced by the pancreas to control the amount of glucose in the bloodstream. People with diabetes either produce too much insulin or not enough.
A worldwide trend in health care reforms and new organizational arrangements focusing on more coordinated and integrated forms of care provision.

Two-way, real-time interactive communication between a patient and a physician or practitioner located at a distant site for the purpose of improving a patient's health through the use of interactive telecommunication equipment that includes, at a minimum, audio and video equipment.
The branch of medicine focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of internal diseases or conditions affecting the internal organs.
A protective, shock-absorbing buffer between each of the vertebra in the spinal column. They also protect nerves that run down the middle of the spine.
An intestinal issue that shows symptoms of constipation, diarrhea and abdominal pain. Irritable bowel syndrome, or IBS, can usually be controlled with lifestyle and diet changes.
An articulation between two bones. Classified primarily by the tissue connecting the bones.
A procedure that removes part or all of the damaged joint and replacing it with artificial implants.
Tests that check a sample of the blood, urine, or body tissues. These samples are then analyzed by a professional to determine whether the results fall within the normal range.
Inflammation of the inner ear or connective nerves from the inner ear to the brain.
A deep cut that leads to the opening of the skin, which often leads to bleeding and severe pain. A laceration requires prompt treatment to limit the risk of infection.

Although slightly different, a lamellar laceration is similar to a corneal perforation and refers to damage that occurs to the cornea, which is typically a fairly serious injury that requires immediate care.
A group of parasites without wings that live on mammals’ scalp, body, or pubic are. Lice are contagious and can spread disease and cause infection when left untreated.

A band of tough connective tissue that holds two bones or pieces of cartilage together in a join. When a ligament is overstretched or torn, it leads to a sprain, which can be painful and require treatment.
Devices or equipment that produce light.
The combination of a lipid and protein whose primary role is transporting blood and other essential fluids throughout the bloodstream.
An essential organ that performs many important functions, including making proteins and blood clotting factors, manufacturing triglycerides and cholesterol, glycogen synthesis, and bile production.
A medical test that aids in diagnosis of liver disease, assessing the severity of known liver disease, and monitoring treatment progress.
Function loss that prevents the liver from performing its normal synthetic and metabolic functions.
A surgical procedure to remove a diseased or injured liver and replace it with a healthy liver from another person.
Low blood pressure happens when blood pressure drops below the normal range and can cause fainting or dizziness.
An abnormal amount of cholesterol in the blood, which can lead to cancer, depression, anxiety, and cardiovascular diseases.
An infection that affects the airways and lungs, such as bronchitis, influenza, pneumonia, and whooping cough.
Any disease that affect the lungs and is often accompanied by breathing problems resulting from the body getting inadequate levels of oxygen.
Small structures that filter out harmful substances in the body. Patients with viral pink eye may have swollen lymph nodes, fever, runny nose, and sore throat.
A severe infection of the mastoid bone, usually caused by a spreading ear infection.
A procedure used to treat chronic ingrown toenails where the doctor removes the growth area of the nail that causes the ingrown toenail
A complicated infection that leads to flu-like symptoms, a fever and a red rash.
Back pain caused by placing undue strain and stress on the vertebral column’s muscles. Usually caused by bad habits, such as bad posture, and can be resolved by correcting such habits.
A type of healthcare facility focused on non-emergency outpatient procedures
Combating a sickness or condition and easing its symptoms.
An inflammation of the brain and spinal cord membranes, usually due to infection (viral, bacterial, or fungal).
A severe headache in which patients often experience a throbbing feeling on one side of their head. Migraines are often chronic and accompanied by reduced vision and nausea.

In essence, this condition combines the worst parts of both tension headaches and migraines. Individuals who suffer from this syndrome often experience both severe tension and pain on one or both sides of their head.
Stands for magnetic resonance imaging scan. Utilizes radio waves and a large magnet to examine organs and structures inside the body.
An infection caused by a staph bacterium that is resistant to the antibiotics typically used to treat a staph infection
A slimy substance found in the sinuses. Mucus serves to protect and lubricate the nasal passageway. An excess of mucus can develop as a reaction to a sinus infection.
Medications that increase muscle mobility while reducing pain and skeletal muscle spasms.
Involuntary muscle contractions that may or may not be painful.
The organ system of our body that muscles, ligaments and tendons belong to. The musculoskeletal system provides support and stability while our body moves.
A procedure done to clear out the sinuses during a sinus infection. It is done using an endoscope, which is a thin, flexible tube with a light and tiny camera.
One of the more common treatment options for a sinus infection. While there are over-the-counter nasal steroid sprays, it is best to ask your primary care provider about nasal steroid spray.
A feeling of discomfort in the body that causes the urge to vomit. It may or may not be followed by actual vomiting. Nausea may be associated with moderate to severe cases of various skin conditions.
Describes an abnormal mass of tissue that forms when cells grow and divide more than they should or do not die when they should. Neoplasia often leads to chronic fevers.
The group of nerves and fibers inside the body that transmit nerve signals is referred to as the nervous system. A deeper cut into the skin can cause nerve damage.
Refers to the neural processes and structure that is required for accurate cognition. Our neurocognitive ability is often altered after a concussion.

Pain that occurs when the nervous system is damaged or not working correctly and can be felt from any of the various levels of the nervous system—the peripheral nerves, the spinal cord, and the brain.
Sodium nitrate is often found in foods such as bacon, sausages and various sandwich meats and is considered by many as a contributing factor to the onset of migraine headaches.
The egg or young form of a parasite, most commonly lice. Nits form the beginning of an infestation and are contagious.
A type of pain caused by damage to body tissue. Nociceptive pain feels sharp, aching, or throbbing.
A type of asthma that occurs from non-allergenic factors, such as viral respiratory infections, exercise, or certain irritants in the air.
Anti-inflammatory drugs that reduce pain and fever, prevent blood clots, and decrease inflammation.
An immature insect that does not develop or grow beyond its initial size. Lice nymphs are similar to nits and can be the beginning of a lice infestation.
An excess storage of body fat.

A form of asthma that occurs when chemical fumes, gases, dust, or other substances are inhaled, typically as part of a job. Individuals who live in areas with high levels of smog and pollution can also acquire occupational asthma.
This term refers to issues dealing with our vision or eyes in general. After a concussion, there is often ‘ocular trauma’ that results and needs to be assessed and properly treated.
An eye injury in which the bone of the eye socket is damaged. In most cases, an orbital fracture occurs due to the blow to the eye, such as being hit by a baseball or punched in the eye.
A condition in which the cartilage (or the hard, slippery tissue covering where the bones form a joint) breaks down.
Also known as over-the-counter medications; considered safe for use by the general public and can be obtained without a prescription
A medical specialist that focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of ear, nose, and throat conditions.
Any form of sexual activity that does not result in penetration and the exchange of fluid.
Pushing the body physically beyond its limits, often resulting in a strain, sprain, or more serious injury.
Weight that is considered above the average when measured through body mass index (BMI) for a person’s age and height.
The release or discharge of an egg from the ovary, which may or may not result in a pregnancy.
The process of providing medical care that alleviates or reduces pain.

A physician who specializes in the evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of pain – has advanced training that qualifies them as your best source of treatment if you are experiencing any type of pain due to illness or injury.
An epidemic of an infectious disease that affects a large region of the world.
A reaction, often called hives, that produces a large number of small, itchy red bumps along the skin.
An organism that feeds off of another organism to attain its benefits and nutrients. Parasites can cause food poisoning in the human body.
A partial thickness burn is also known as a second-degree burn, and it is more serious than a superficial burn, as it causes damage to layers of skin deeper than the first.
A thick, sticky mucus that develops with most illnesses or irritation of the respiratory tract.
A routine test a primary care doctor performs to check a person’s overall health.
A type of specialist that uses passive and active therapies to improve a patient’s range of movement and reduce the amount of pain they experience.
An inflammation or infection of the conjunctiva. This condition may be caused by various factors and is extremely contagious.
An infection or inflammation of the conjunctiva, or the outer membrane of the inner eyelid and eyeball. May form a crust of discharge on the eyelashes during the nighttime.
A condition in which the pleura, two large thin layers of tissue that separate your lungs from your chest wall, become inflamed.
An infection that occurs when the air sacs in one or both lungs become inflamed due to severe sickness. The air sacs also become filled with fluid or pus, making it difficult to breathe.
One of the main causes of contact dermatitis. Poison ivy, which is found in nature, is a plant that generally causes a severe itch and can even be painful in more severe cases.
An allergic reaction to the oily coating covering the poison ivy plant. Poison ivy dermatitis can occur even after indirect contact with the plant.
A term that describes a substance that can cause harm or death when consumed by the body.

A condition in which a patient’s blood sugar level is higher than normal without being high enough for an official diabetes diagnosis. By treating prediabetes, patients can prevent contracting diabetes.
A physician’s authorization for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.
Helps detect or prevent serious diseases and medical problems before they can become major, such as annual check-ups, immunizations, and flu shots.
The action of stopping something from happening or arising; in healthcare, prevention refers to preventing the development or spread of disease.
This type of migraine treatment focuses on treating frequently-occuring migraines. The treatment strives to help decrease the frequency of headaches and the severity.
The absence of disease, either by preventing the occurrence of a disease or by halting a disease and averting resulting complications after its onset.
A primary care physician provides comprehensive care to a patient and tends to be a person’s main point of contact for general medical care and specialist referrals
Medical services that provide comprehensive healthcare for patients and support their overall wellness.
Medical services that provide comprehensive healthcare for patients and support their overall wellness.

Aims to prevent disease or injury before it ever occurs. This is done by preventing exposures to hazards that cause disease or injury, altering unhealthy or unsafe behaviours that can lead to disease or injury, and increasing resistance to disease or injury should exposure occur.
A condition in which symptoms will only get worse.
The use of talk therapy to help increase happiness, change behavior, and overcome problems.
A physician who specializes in treating respiratory tract diseases. A patient may be referred to a pulmonologist if they are experiencing asthmatic symptoms or difficulty breathing.
A bacterial infection that occurs due to inflammation of the substances in the kidney, often the result of a UTI.
A highly recommended course of treatment for many sprains and strains. The R.I.C.E. method stands for rest, ice, compression and elevation.
A rapid antigen detection test used to diagnose strep throat. Involves swabbing the throat and analyzing the swab.
A skin rash is a temporary red, bumpy surface-level injury that occurs due to an underlying disease, hot and humid weather, excess sun exposure, or scratchy clothes.
The restoration of good health or a normal life resulting from therapy or treatment following imprisonment, an addiction, or an illness.
A method of healthcare delivery that uses the latest advances in information technology to gather patient data outside of traditional healthcare settings.
Small droplets consisting of saliva, mucus, and other matter from respiratory tract surfaces.
A specialist that treats and provides emergency care to patients having trouble breathing or suffering from cardiac or pulmonary diseases.
A disease that can affect the heart, joints, brain, and skin that can develop if strep throat is not treated properly.
A condition in which the immune system attacks the joints, starting with the joints’ lining.
Commonly referred to as a runny nose; excess fluid containing clear fluid or thick mucus that runs down the nasal passages.
A virus that causes the common cold.
A risk factor is something that increases a person’s risk of developing a disease or infection.
The most common cause of vomiting and diarrhea in toddlers. The rotavirus is not often dangerous in itself, but it can lead to dehydration, which is especially concerning in toddlers.
This term refers to a sudden opening of a part of the body and often leads to severe bleeding and pain. A rupture in the eye typically occurs due to a cut or a blow to the eye.
A laboratory test done by taking a sample of the patient’s saliva. These tests can detect the presence of HIV, hepatitis C, and HPV.
A simple and safe home remedy often used for sore throats.
A bacterial illness featuring a bright red rash accompanied by a sore throat and high fever; it develops in some people who have strep.
One of the largest nerves, which extends from the lower end of the spinal cord down the back of the thigh and divides above the knee joint.

Pain that radiates along the sciatic nerve and down the back of the leg. It may travel all the way to the foot, and it is usually felt in the buttocks. Commonly associated with conditions such as degenerative disc disease, herniated discs, and lumbar spinal stenosis.
A condition in which the patient’s spine has an abnormal, sideways curvature. May be caused by congenital, developmental, or degenerative problems. May also have no apparent cause at all.
A flat, surface-level injury caused by rubbing the skin against a hard surface such as cement or asphalt.
A type of high blood pressure caused by another medical condition that affects the kidneys, arteries, heart, or endocrine system.
Aims to reduce the impact of a disease or injury that has already occurred by detecting and treating disease or injury.
A disease caused by an infection due to a bacteria, virus, or parasite that invades the body through sexual intercourse.

A skin condition caused by a viral infection. Shingles results in a painful rash that may occur anywhere on the body. However, it most typically appears as a single stripe of blisters wrapping around the side of the torso.
Describes and unhealty condition of mind and/or body.
Also known as sinusitis, an inflammation of the tissue lining the sinuses.
A connected system of air-filled cavities inside of your skull. Healthy sinuses allow for the free flow of air and drainage of excess mucus in the sinuses.
Also referred to as a sinus infection, sinusitis is a condition where the nasal passages are inflamed, often caused by some other virus, such as the common cold or the flu.
A term used to describe the tearing away of a patch of skin. A skin avulsion can occur as a result of various cuts and body trauma. It often needs medical assistance to repair.
A term used to describe various types of rashes, burns, and other issues affecting the skin.
An abnormal area on the surface of the body that has become damaged due to an insect bite or sting, wound, ulcer, abscess, or tumor.
A relative force that prevents something from slipping or moving easily.
Throat pain or irritation that can occur with or without swallowing and often accompanies infections, such as a cold or flu.
A type of chiropractic therapy where the specialist applies a controlled thrust to a joint of the spine. Also known as spinal manipulative therapy or HVLA.
A gentler form of chiropractic therapy where the specialist utilizes slow movement to mobilize the joint.
A pre-participation physical examination that helps to determine whether or not a person physically able to participate in a sport safely.

A stretching or tearing of a ligament, which is the fibrous tissue in our bodies that connects our bones and our joints. A sprain can happen anywhere there is a ligament, but it most commonly occurs to an ankle, wrist or knee.
Showing no activity; dull and sluggish.
Contrary to popular belief, the stomach flu is not at all related to influenza. Instead, it is merely a misleading term that refers to an intestinal infection.
A sore that develops on the lining of the stomach, caused by stomach acid. Stomach ulcers usually create a moderate to severe level of abdominal pain.
A method by which healthcare providers share patient medical information like lab reports, imaging studies, videos, and other records with a physician, radiologist, or specialist at another location.
A force or pressure exerted on a part of the body to an extreme or dangerous degree; a strained muscle is the product of strenuous activity or accidental tear from pulling or stretching.
An infection of the throat and tonsils caused by a bacteria that presents as a sore throat accompanied by a fever.
The bacterium that causes strep throat, also known as group A streptococcus.
Stress is a change that causes psychological, physical, or emotional strain.
A method of testing in which a person walks on a treadmill or pedals on a stationary bike, and their heart activity is tracked and measured.
An eye injury in which the white surface of the eye becomes red and filled with blood. It occurs when a blood vessel bursts.
A superficial burn is a common term used to describe a first-degree burn. A superficial burn is usually not serious and only damages the top layer of skin.
Likely to be harmed or under the influence of something in particular.
An abnormal enlargement of a body part.
A respiratory infection that was first recognized in the 1919 influenza pandemic.
A form of medication determined to help with the symptoms caused by a condition, particularly one that affects the head area, such as migraines.
Disease or condition that affects the entire body rather than just one part.
Communication over a distance by cable, telegraph, telephone, or broadcasting.
The remote diagnosis and treatment of patients by means of telecommunications technology.
A condition that produces pain and compromised jaw joint and muscle movement.
Flexible fibrous collagen tissue that connects a muscle to a bone. Although a tendon is flexible, it typically is not elastic and can overstretch or tear during intense exercise.

A headache that often feels as if there is a tight band wrapped around the individual’s head. They often are considered mild to moderate and can often be treated with appropriate pain relief medication.
A severe bacterial infection that can cause severe pain and muscle spasms.
A laboratory diagnostic test that looks for any bacterial or fungal infection in the throat. Conducted by swabbing the throat and placing the sample into a culture that allows infections to grow.
Butterfly-shaped endocrine gland in the neck that makes hormones and plays a role in metabolism.
A surgical procedure in which the tonsils are removed.
An inflammation of the two lymph nodes in the back of the throat, the tonsils; the condition can be caused by the bacterium that causes strep throat.
A pair of soft tissue masses at the back of the throat. Each is covered with pink mucosa.

A severe injury to the body classified as either blunt force trauma or penetrating trauma. Blunt force trauma describes an injury that involves an object striking the body while penetrating trauma describes an injury that consists of an object piercing through the body.
A trigger can be a number of different things and is considered anything that leads to the onset of a migraine headache. For many, this includes certain foods, smells or stressful activities.
A type of diabetes where the pancreas produces too little insulin or none at all. This condition typically appears in adolescence or younger, but it can also develop in adults.
A type of diabetes where the body either resists insulin’s effects or fails to produce enough insulin to maintain normal blood sugar levels. This condition typically appears in adulthood.
This condition is a type of inflammatory bowel disease that causes ulcers and inflammation in the lining of the large intestine.
An unexpected drop in weight when a person is not actively trying to lose weight.
A three-step examination program for medical licensure in the United States.
A viral infection that affects parts of the body that are higher than the lungs, including the nose, sinuses, and throat.
A vital part of the urinary system. The urethra works to deliver urine out of the body. In men, the urethra is also responsible for delivering semen. The urethra is commonly affected during a UTI.
A urine test that checks for the presence of disease, drugs, urinary tract infections, kidney problems, diabetes, and more.
The system of the body that consists of the ureters, kidneys, bladder, and the urethra.
An infection in the urinary system.
A biological concoction that provides the patient with active acquired immunity to a specific infectious disease.
A poisonous substance that can cause disease and, in severe cases, death when injected into the bloodstream.

One of the 33 interlocking bones forming the spinal column. Has three primary functional components: vertebral body, vertebral arch, and transverse processes. The vertebral body bears loads, the vertebral arch protects the spinal cord, and the transverse processes attach ligaments.
A sudden sensation of dizziness and loss of balance often caused by disease affecting the inner ear or the vestibular nerve.
A sac found on skin that is either filled with fluid or air. A vesicle occurs on top of a rash. Most commonly, vesicles exist as a result of a heat rash.
The sensory system that is largely responsible for our ability to balance ourselves. After a concussion, our vestibular system often is affected, causing a loss of balance and coordination.

A virus is a microscopic organism that invades and reproduces inside of the body. The act of this invasion is referred to as a viral infection, which often causes illness such as influenza or the common cold.

A very small organism that consumes living cells to reproduce. They often cause an illness in which the body has to fight off. The sooner treatment can be administered, the easier it is for the body to fight off a virus.
A major symptom of a concussion. This is dizziness that results from constant movement or changing environmental patterns. It is often accompanied by a loss of balance.
Vital signs are clinical measurements of the body’s essential functions.
A loss in body weight through voluntary or involuntary means.
A neck injury commonly associated with car accidents, especially rear-end collisions. It can result in mild to severe injuries.
A syndrome whereby a patient’s feeling of anxiety in a medical environment results in an abnormally high reading when their blood pressure is measured.
A serious, highly contagious respiratory tract infection that can be prevented by a vaccine.
A type of electromagnetic radiation used to generate images of internal bodily structures and tissues.

A form of penetrating, high-energy electromagnetic radiation that can pass through the body. X-rays are most often used to examine the bones and joints, though they may sometimes be used to detect any problems affecting soft tissues.
